title: Round 8 stream A: the laser's burn marks lie on the floor once their rock burns, the pets stand on the island slabs, and the hull pushes the friendlies aside
context: Owner, 2026-11-05, notes 1-3 on 9625441f (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-round-8-seven-notes-design.md, stream A): 1) 'when SOL burns with the laser, the burned marks that remain for a few seconds should be on the ground level; currently they hover at the higher level of where the rocks used to be'; 2) 'cheetah and other pets clip through the ground, at least through the base under the Stalheart, they should be above'; 3) 'collision between friendly units: the tank bumping into mechs, cheetah, etc. should push them aside'. Branch round-8-ground off d67d5fb7, port 18181, owner asleep: every decision below is the agent's, written down to be overturned in one line.
outcome:
NOTE 1, MEASURED FIRST on the game path (scratch note1.mjs: ?stage=6&phase=expedition&laser=online, a pass, the seat, the beam steered onto the nearest rock and held; the 'Laser scorch' instance matrices read through the renderer's scene, 753 m to the unit): BEFORE, one rock burn left 9 stamps, 2 at the rock's top (4.0 m over the floor) and 4 on a ramp at 0.8 / 1.6 / 2.4 / 3.2 m: the stamps laid while the contact stood on the rock, and the gap the next aim filled from the ribbon's last point (the rock's top) down to the floor. The ramp is the larger half of the hover, which the scout had not seen. AFTER: all 5 stamps of the same burn at the floor's own lift (radius 1.000053), 2 stamps laid again. HOW: src/fx/scorch-trail.js keeps each slot's ground point and normal and gains reseat(groundAt), which rewrites only the matrix's translation of every live stamp whose ground moved (turn, size, age and seed untouched); src/fx/orbital-laser.js reseat() re-seats the ribbon's `last` point too (that is what kills the ramp); src/fx/laser-arsenal.js calls it with its own groundAt right after host.breakCells, so a kit wall burned through re-seats as well; state().laser.reseated counts the moves. td-tab untouched. --laser-game green (rock 1, the slowest break 4.4 ms).
NOTE 2, MEASURED FIRST (scratch note2.mjs: ?pets=born, 75 game s sampled every 250 ms, two runs; state().companions.units[].underM, the metres the drawn wrap sits under the floor): BEFORE, C-07 and K0-TECH up to 0.96 m inside the slabs, RECKON K9 0.6 m, the mech 0.23 m, under by more than 1 cm in 21-81 % of the samples. AFTER, 0 for all four (277 and 147 samples a unit). The scout's '1.1 m at the edge, 2 m at the corners' was the half diagonal's sag counted for the side: by the geometry the 57 x 56 m Stålheart slab on the 753 m planet sinks 0.54 m at its side and 1.06 m at its corner; the kit's foundation_slab.glb tops out at y 0 (a 0.28 m plate and a 1.2 m skirt below), so the slab's top IS the island's tangent plane and no thickness is added. HOW: src/domain/slab-floor.js plateFloor(p, plates), the radial factor onto the highest plate whose rectangle holds p (1 elsewhere), tested; src/fx/story-base.js floorAt(p) builds the plates from each grown island's own drawn frame (basisAt, top); src/fx/companions.js draws the wrap at pos x floorAt(pos) (seat(), in the walk and the print bed) while the play's point stays on the sphere; td-tab hands floorAt on the existing host line. NOT CHECKED: whether the hull itself reads under a slab's edge (the spec's 'note it'); no screenshot was taken.
NOTE 3, MEASURED FIRST (scratch note3.mjs: the hull put down on each pet's cell for 2 s, then aimed at each from 8-40 m and driven 5 s with W; state().companions.units[].inHullFrames, frames a born unit's point stood inside the hull's box grown by its pad): BEFORE (a 5 x 2.5 m half-size box, before the hull's own size was read), C-07 19 frames inside parked (1.1 m deep), the mech 81 parked and 32 driven (5.8 m deep), K0-TECH 13 driven and 60 next to the parked hull at the start; the dodge kept C-07 and RECKON K9 out on the drive. The drawn hull's box, read through creatures.hull(): half 4.4 x 2.19 m. AFTER (box 4.4 x 2.2, pad 0.8 m, the mech's padM 4): 0 frames inside for all four on the same probe; C-07 shoved 51 times by the drive, the mech 12, K0-TECH 56 by the parked hull. The Ridgebacks (?reinforce=1, landed, the hull put on each one's cell 2 s): pushed 95 / 93 / 0 / 1 times (the two arena mechs keep walking into the parked hull and slide along its side). HOW: src/domain/friendly-push.js pushOut(p, hull, { halfLength, halfWidth, pad, free }) (the hull's tangent frame, src/domain/hull-bodies.js boxContact for the least move, 1.001 over it so the sphere's re-projection leaves nothing inside, the box's other sides in turn when the caller's free() refuses: on the roam and off the buildings) and inHull, tested on the four sides, a corner, the heading, free(); COMPANIONS.hull { halfLength 4.4, halfWidth 2.2, pad 0.8 }; companions.js pushes every born, loaded unit after its step, greeting or not, and lets a unit shoved off the roam walk back onto it; the cats' greet.nearM 3 -> 6.5 m (half length + pad + 1, rounded up: 3 m sat a greeting cat inside the hull); mech-squad.js pushes a Ridgeback's drawn position (REINFORCEMENTS.hullPadM 3: the MX-06's 6 m plot at 0.75) and re-lays a segment under way from the pushed point; its cells and records untouched. td-tab: hullDir() on the companions' and the squad's existing host lines (5,329 lines, unchanged). The hull is not slowed or turned.
alternatives: Note 1: seat every stamp on the floor at stamp time (groundAt ignores rock): rejected, a burn on a rock that has not broken yet would draw its scorch inside the rock; the stamps stay where the contact stood and are laid again when the ground under them drops.

Note 1: re-seat only the stamps over the broken cells: rejected as needless, one reseat walks at most 1000 live stamps through the voxel-hash cellAt once per break batch (the slowest break measured 4.4 ms in --laser-game, unchanged).

Note 2: lift the play's own point (u.pos) onto the slab: rejected, the roam, the play's distances, the hull's keep-off and the print bed all read u.pos on the unit sphere; only the drawn wrap is lifted.
Note 2: smooth the step off a slab's edge: not done, the drop is the slab's real edge (its 1.2 m skirt) and the pets walk off it as off a kerb; the owner can ask for a ramp.
Note 3: slow or deflect the hull on a pet: rejected by the spec and the owner ('push them aside').

Note 3: the hull box read live off the drawn tank (src/fx/hull-contact.js hullAt): it exists only under the Pearl set's bodies; the companions and the Ridgebacks read the measured half sizes from COMPANIONS.hull instead (4.4 x 2.2 m, the harness's own hl/hw of the story's hull).

Note 3, the Ridgebacks: pushing their cells (cur/next) instead of the drawn position: rejected as intrusive; the drawn position is pushed and a segment under way is re-laid from it, their records and cells untouched.
evidence: scratch/r8-ground (not committed): note1.mjs (the scorch's instance radii through a rock burn), note2.mjs (underM over 75 game s), note3.mjs / note3-after.mjs (park and drive), mk-probe.sh, their logs note2-before.log, note3-before.log, note3-after.log, suite-*.log
npm test (330 programs), npm run check, npm run architecture (td-tab 5329 / 5450)

browser, STALHEART_BROWSER_PORT=18181 under the lock: --laser-game green after note 1 (rock 1, the slowest break 4.4 ms); --companions three runs on the final code: green, red once on its pre-existing dodge assertion ('k9 dodged': the picked K9 was dashing when the hull came, closest 3.53 m, 0 dodges; companion-play and the dodge are untouched by this stream; the likely cause, not proven, is a slow headless frame moving the 38 m/s hull past companions.js HULL_JUMP 8 m, which zeroes the hull velocity the dodge reads), then green with the new round 8 assertions (underM 0 for all four, 0 frames in the hull, K0-TECH pushed 53 times); --pet-print green (the four prints on their beds, pet-print and pet-print-arena). Not run: the Ridgeback suites (--reinforcements, --wire); the Ridgebacks were checked by the scratch probe only (note3-after.log).
